description: For a week, protesters have faced off against heavily armed ICE agents outside Delaney Hall in Newark, NJ, in some of the most intense immigration enforcement confrontations in recent history. A senator was gassed. A protester was Tased on train tracks. Families were turned away. Pro-Trump counter-protesters arrived to cheer the agents on.

faqs.answer: On Monday, May 26, Sen. Andy Kim was caught in a cloud of pepper spray while standing near protesters outside Delaney Hall. He was attempting to de-escalate tensions. DHS claimed pepper balls 'did not strike anyone directly.'
faqs.question: What happened to Sen. Andy Kim?

faqs.answer: Protests began Sunday, May 25, when families formed a human chain to block a detainee transfer. By Tuesday night, ICE agents were chasing protesters across streets, Tasing one on train tracks, and spraying journalists. On Thursday, reports emerged of agents beating hunger strikers inside. On Friday, state police in riot gear clashed with protesters after the governor established a 'protest zone.'
faqs.question: How have the clashes escalated?

faqs.answer: Yes. Republican organizations including the Montclair Republicans and America First Republicans of New Jersey organized a 'Support ICE' rally on Saturday, May 30, with congressional and Senate candidates attending. Pro-Trump counter-protesters have been present throughout the week, at times standing between ICE agents and anti-ICE demonstrators.
faqs.question: Are there counter-protests?

faqs.answer: The anti-ICE protesters include families of detainees, immigrant rights organizations (Make the Road New Jersey, New Jersey Alliance for Immigrant Justice, Eyes On ICE NJ, Resistencia en Accion), faith leaders, Democratic elected officials, and mutual aid organizers who have been providing food and medical supplies at the site for months.
faqs.question: Who are the protesters?

faqs.answer: Gov. Mikie Sherrill sent state police to establish a protected protest zone on Friday, May 29, after days of clashes. She called the situation unsafe and said she would not give ICE 'a pretext to expand operations in our state.' On Friday night, state police in riot gear clashed with protesters who refused to leave the designated zone.
faqs.question: What has the governor's response been?

leadParagraph: A week of sustained protests outside Delaney Hall immigration detention center in Newark, NJ has seen federal agents pepper-spray a sitting U.S. senator, Tase a protester on train tracks, and beat hunger-striking detainees inside with batons. Families of detainees have been turned away while pro-Trump counter-protesters organize rallies supporting ICE, creating dueling demonstrations in a confrontation that mirrors America's deep divide over immigration.

methodology: Reported using open-source intelligence including on-scene reporting from The Guardian, Gothamist, CBS New York, WHYY, CNN, ABC7, NBC, TIME, The Independent, Patch, and Insider NJ. Congressional and gubernatorial statements. Advocacy organizations. DHS and DOJ official statements. Reporting period: May 23–30, 2026.
title: The Siege of Delaney Hall: A Week of Clashes, Families in Agony, and the Machine That Crushes Protest
